newsitem.title: GERMANY: Muted Q1 sales growth for German chemical sector.
newsitem.headline: Muted Q1 sales growth for German chemical sector.

text.p: Sales in the German chemicals industry rose by a muted 1.5 percent to 55.5 billion marks in the first quarter of 1997, the chemical sector employers' group BAVC said on Wednesday.

Foreign sales advanced 7.5 percent to 25.6 billion marks while domestic sales, continuing a phase of weakness, dropped three percent to just under 30 billion, the association said in a research paper.

Employment levels in the sector also dropped by 2.9 percent to around 507,100 staff, although the BAVC said the pace of job losses had slowed from last year, when some 10 percent of east German jobs were lost.
Net output in the industry was on average four percent higher in the first four months of the year than in the year-ago period.
Domestic producer prices fell on average by 0.3 percent in the first four months, but the downward pressure on prices was easing, the group said. Prices actually rose 0.4 percent in April.
Productivity rose seven percent in the first quarter while unit wage costs fell four percent, the BAVC said.

Looking ahead, the group cited a forecast published last month by the European chemical industry association, which predicted 2.5 percent growth for the German chemicals sector this year, in line with the European Union average.
